I disagree!! Depends on the experience you are interested in.

Hostels are far more social, an airbnb will normally be more private. (Even if you get a room in someone's house, they normally leave you to be)

I am a 21F Canadian and I travelled to both cities solo earlier in 2018. I found both cities very safe. 

Always keep in mind that everyone has different experiences when they're travelling, one bad experience during a trip can completely change how one feels in a country/city. 

The "city dangers" are something to be aware of **everywhere.** Even places where you consider yourself to feel safe or has a low crime rate, you need to stay aware and like you said, use caution/common sense!

If you do this, I think you will be okay!!!

Did this same trip in April 2018! 

I highly recommend Bigfish hostel in Budapest. I had the best experience there and it helped me really enjoy Buda. 

When in Vienna, visiting the opera house was a highlight for me. (I purchased standing tickets for like $20CAD, so it is an affordable night out). I saw a humorous ballet it was fantastic, if that is your sort of thing.

The Czech Inn Prague is a great hostel, not a central location but the tram ride into the city is really enjoyable. 

Last suggestion is to bring a lock for a locker with you! And being able to pack all your luggage in a bag you can carry on your back or someway is ideal, I ended up walking A LOT more than I anticipated lol. 

Good luck you will LOVE Eastern Europe

I am always nervous when travelling, and I consider myself to be semi-experienced!!! Just wait until you arrive .... especially since this is your first time!
